text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- After months of delay, the first electronics/electrical industry waste management plant in central Negeri Sembilan has started operations.

-- The government will study a report by Tenaga Nasional on whether to compensate consumers for losses suffered during the Aug 3 blackout, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad. Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Saturday compensation for power disruption was not practised by most countries.
-- The 1997 Budget will focus on reducing the current account deficit and attracting high-techonology industries to help increase exports, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
-- Malaysian courts must pass sentences which reflect the gravity of ofences to ensure that a mockery is not made of if the judicial system, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
